mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome. I’m so glad you’re here with me, ready to dive into a journey that reveals some of the most powerful truths about education in America. Imagine standing at the edge of two neighborhoods—just a few miles apart—yet their schools feel worlds away from each other. That’s the contrast Jonathan Kozol explores in his eye-opening book, Savage Inequalities: Children in America's Schools. Together, we’ll uncover stories of classrooms struggling with limited resources, crumbling buildings, and dreams that sometimes feel out of reach. But we’ll also witness the hope, resilience, and quiet determination of students and teachers who show up every day, no matter the odds. As we step into these realities side by side, we’ll see how issues like race, class, and geography can shape the opportunities children have—or don’t have. This isn’t just about numbers or policies—it’s about real lives, and what it truly means when educational justice is denied. So, let’s set out together, ready to understand, reflect, and maybe see things a little differently. There’s a lot to discover—and it matters more than ever.
